panels: Use case: illustration-story. First panel of a three-panel cartoon comic introduction for the cosy magical browser game 'Le monde tient dans une valise'. One old CLOSED caramel brown leather travel suitcase with rounded corners, brass latches and brass corner protectors, on a wooden table in a tiny warm attic. A shaft of golden afternoon sun catches dust motes. Nearby only a folded blank map and a little rolled paper, no other luggage. A sense of a wonderful discovery about to happen. Hand-painted cartoon comic, confident thick dark brown outlines, rounded expressive shapes, rich gouache texture, warm honey cream and moss green palette. Same painted illustration style as a whimsical fantasy storybook, never photorealistic, no 3D. Wide landscape composition with the suitcase as the clear central subject, generous framing. No people, no words, no letters, no numbers, no speech bubbles, no panel border: game will render comic frames and localized narration separately.

Second panel of the same three-panel cartoon comic. Image 1 is the previous attic panel: preserve its world, warm painted comic style, wooden table, honey sunlight and suitcase identity. Image 2 is a design reference ONLY for the open suitcase's green lining and compass integrated into its lid. Show the same suitcase now OPEN on the same table, revealing emerald green velvet and a big brass compass built into the upright lid, with exactly TWO slender needles, one turquoise and one violet. Soft turquoise and gold magical ribbons curl upward from its empty lower compartment. A few papers lift gently in the magic. View from the front, slightly above, full suitcase visible, lid and bottom mechanically coherent. Thick expressive dark brown cartoon outlines and gouache texture, playful wonder, more comic than realism. No people, no standalone compass, no third needle, no text, no writing, no numbers, no speech bubbles, no panel border. Wide landscape image matching the first panel's aspect ratio.

Third and final panel of this cosy cartoon comic introduction. The same caramel leather and brass suitcase on the warm attic table, same green lining and brass compass integrated into its upright lid. A joyful magical panorama now unfurls above its open lower compartment: a ribbon of paper winding into tiny dreamlike blue islands, rounded snowy peaks and a whimsical forest, like miniature worlds floating from a travel journal. The attic softly recedes behind the colourful vision. A sense of invitation, discovery and a world of possibility, no danger. Match the first panel's thick dark brown comic outlines, rich gouache paint, honey sunlight and rounded storybook shapes. Wide landscape composition. The suitcase remains recognizable and mechanically coherent. No people, no text, no writing, no numbers, no speech bubbles, no panel frame. Do not show ingredient recipes or additional controls.
